headline: GOLD -1.9% TO $4,025, SILVER -2.9% TO $57.29 — Dollar Surges On Hot PCE Data; August 7 Payrolls Is Next Break Catalyst
snippet: Gold and silver sold off sharply on August 1, 2026, as the US dollar surged to a three-week high following a US personal spending report that came in hotter than economists forecast — the PCE data matched inflation expectations but the spending acceleration dialled back the probability of a September rate cut from roughly 50% to near 30%, and the dollar moved accordingly. US gold futures for August delivery dropped 1.9% to $4,025.10, while spot gold settled near $4,043/oz; spot silver fell 2.9% to $57.29/oz. The drop came despite gold posting its first monthly gain since February — approximately 0.5% for July — following the Federal Reserve's July 29 decision to hold rates at 3.5–3.75% on a 9-3 vote, with three members calling for an additional 25bp hike. Mexico-listed silver miners including Fresnillo fell more than the metal itself, reflecting the operating leverage that amplifies both gains and losses for producers. The SPDR Gold Shares ETF and iShares Silver Trust both declined in sympathy. Despite the session weakness, the technical picture for gold remains constructive above $4,000/oz — a level buy-program activity has defended on each test. The August 7 US non-farm payrolls report is now the critical macro catalyst: a soft jobs number would revive the rate-cut narrative, weaken the dollar, and quickly push gold back toward $4,100–$4,200 and silver above $59. A strong print would do the opposite and potentially test gold's $4,000 structural support for the first time in three weeks. Junior mining investors should watch August 7 closely as the payrolls result will likely set the sector's trajectory for the remainder of the month.

headline: 1911 GOLD BAKER TARGET: 36.44 g/t Au OVER 1.1m — Third Near-Mine Zone Opens At True North Manitoba (TSXV: AUMB)
snippet: 1911 Gold Corporation (TSXV: AUMB, OTCQB: AUMBF) reported assay results on July 30, 2026 from its surface and underground exploration drill program at the True North Gold Project in southeastern Manitoba, confirming a new high-grade zone called Baker and extending two previously known targets — SAM Southeast and Shore — to a combined mineralized system now traced over 720 metres of strike and approaching 975 metres of depth. The headline Baker intercept: hole TN-26-076 returned 36.44 g/t gold over 1.1 metres, including 73.70 g/t Au over 0.5 metres. At SAM Southeast, hole TN-26-094 hit 15.89 g/t Au over 2.70 metres (including 40.1 g/t over 1.0m), and at Shore, hole TN-26-088 returned 5.99 g/t Au over 4.9 metres (including 24.9 g/t over 0.7m). The program comprised 20 surface diamond holes totalling 5,017 metres and 10 underground holes totalling 3,560 metres as resource definition drilling. The discovery of Baker — a new zone not previously part of the resource outline — is the significant item here for investors. Near-mine discovery at an active producing project immediately reduces capital intensity to reach ore: if Baker can be connected to existing underground workings at True North, the economics of extraction are far better than a greenfield target at the same grade. For TSX-V investors tracking Manitoba gold, 1911 Gold's systematic near-mine drilling philosophy is producing exactly the kind of step-function discovery that changes resource inventory narratives — and the Baker intersection at 73.70 g/t gold in the visible gold range puts it in the top tier of high-grade underground intercepts announced in Canada this summer.

headline: CAPSTONE COPPER: $354M EBITDA, SEVENTH RECORD QUARTER — Mantoverde C1 $0.86/lb; Revenue $739M, +36% YoY (TSX: CS)
snippet: Capstone Copper Corp. (TSX: CS, ASX: CSC) reported its seventh consecutive quarterly record on July 30, 2026, posting Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $354 million — up 64% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter — alongside revenue of $739.7 million (+36% YoY) and operating cash flow of $259.7 million (+22% YoY). The standout operational performance came from Mantoverde in Chile, which reached record throughput of 36,300 tonnes per day (13% above design capacity) while achieving a C1 cash cost of $0.86 per pound of copper — the lowest in the mine's history and one of the most competitive production costs of any copper operation globally at current throughput. Mantoverde alone produced 23,485 tonnes of copper in Q2 including 18,190 tonnes of copper sulphides at the $0.86/lb C1. On a consolidated basis, Capstone produced 51,759 tonnes of copper in Q2 at a C1 cost of $2.82 per pound. At spot copper near $6.00/lb, a $2.82/lb consolidated C1 cost implies a gross production margin of approximately $3.18/lb — among the widest in Capstone's history and validating the company's 2022–2025 capital programme at Mantoverde. For junior copper developer investors watching the commodity cycle, Capstone's seventh consecutive quarterly record provides further validation that $5.50–$6.50/lb copper is the new structural price band for copper, not an anomaly, which materially improves the project-level economics on development assets that were marginal at $3.50 copper in 2023.

headline: PUREPOINT URANIUM NOVA: 5.6m AT 53,300 CPS — Summer Program Confirms High-Grade Athabasca Expansion (TSXV: PTU)
snippet: Purepoint Uranium Group Inc. (TSXV: PTU, OTCQX: PTUUF) reported results from the first phase of its 2026 summer drill program at the Nova Discovery on the Dorado Project — a 50/50 joint venture with IsoEnergy Ltd. (TSX: IE) in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — with the final hole of the phase, NV26-11, intersecting 5.6 metres of continuous radioactivity averaging 11,730 counts per second (cps) and peaking at 53,300 cps from the downhole probe. The reading is consistent with the high-grade uranium mineralization that characterized the winter 2026 program, which had produced peaks up to 73,100 cps and laboratory-confirmed assay grades of up to 8.1% U3O8 at the Nova Discovery. Laboratory assays from NV26-11 are currently pending. Purepoint is drilling the summer program — seven holes targeting approximately 3,150 metres — to further expand and define the Nova Discovery ahead of the resource estimate that will formally characterize the system's tonnage and grade. The Athabasca Basin is the world's highest-grade uranium district, and the eastern margin sub-basin hosting Dorado has produced several significant discoveries in the past decade. For uranium investors, the key metric at this stage is whether 53,300 cps represents a widening or a narrowing of the previously intersected high-grade core — that answer comes with the assays. What is confirmed is that radioactivity is continuous across 5.6 metres, which implies mineralisation is spatially coherent and not just a thin streak. The Nova Discovery is in a size and grade class that warrants continued attention from investors tracking the Athabasca exploration cycle.

headline: FANCAMP SPLITS INTO GOLDERA — $5.5M Financing Complete; Two New TSX-V Stocks (GERA + ERDA) Debut August 5
snippet: Fancamp Exploration completed the spin-out of all of its core mineral exploration assets into Goldera Exploration on July 30, 2026, via a court-approved plan of arrangement — creating two separate public companies that will both commence trading on the TSX Venture Exchange at market open on August 5, 2026. Goldera (TSXV: GERA) becomes the exploration vehicle, having closed a concurrent $5.5 million financing and receiving all of Fancamp's mineral exploration portfolio. Fancamp itself has been renamed to ERDA Resource Opportunities Inc. (TSXV: ERDA) and will pursue a different mandate as an investment-oriented issuer post-transaction. The spin-out structure reflects a growing trend in junior mining: separation of exploration assets from holding or investment company structures to improve capital allocation clarity, create pure-play exposure for exploration investors, and unlock value that can be obscured when a company serves multiple mandates simultaneously. Goldera's management team and the exploration assets it carries (land packages, technical data, optionality) will be the focus once it begins trading. For investors watching the TSX-V listing calendar, the August 5 debut of both GERA and ERDA creates a new entry point into the story — the first week of trading for a spun-out exploration vehicle often sees elevated volume as former Fancamp shareholders decide whether to hold, sell, or average up in the pure-play exploration company.

headline: FIREFLY METALS PEA IMMINENT — 42m At 6.1% CuEq Reshapes Green Bay Restart Economics; FFM Joins ASX 200 (TSX/ASX: FFM)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / FireFly Metals Ltd.
snippet: FireFly Metals Ltd. (TSX: FFM, ASX: FFM, OTC: FFMFF) is entering August with two significant catalysts converging: a Preliminary Economic Assessment and Scoping Study targeting the Green Bay Copper-Gold Project in Newfoundland for release this month, and a recent addition to the S&P/ASX 200 index — an index inclusion that widens the company's institutional shareholder base and signals market recognition of its growing scale. The PEA is being built around extraordinary drilling results from the project's Core Zone, which contains approximately 20 million tonnes grading near 4% copper equivalent. The two most recent published headline intersections — 42.0 metres grading 6.1% CuEq and 51.5 metres grading 4.9% CuEq — represent the kind of consistently high-grade thick intercepts that rarely appear in Newfoundland copper projects and that underpin early-production economics. Green Bay's prior history as a producing mine (previously operated by Teck and others) also means existing permits, infrastructure, and underground access reduce early-stage capital requirements significantly compared to a true greenfield project. The PEA, previously guided for mid-2026, was shifted to August to incorporate the dramatically improved Core Zone results — the additional delay suggests management believes the Core Zone data changes the entire development scenario materially enough to warrant the revised economic modelling. For investors tracking high-grade copper development in Canada's Atlantic provinces at a moment when copper sits at historically elevated prices above $6/lb, FireFly Metals' August PEA release is arguably the most significant pending copper study in the junior-to-mid-tier tier.

headline: VISTA GOLD AT DIGGERS & DEALERS — Mt Todd NT Permits Advance, Dewatering Begins, 2027 Design On Track (NYSE: VGZ)
snippet: Vista Gold Corp. (NYSE American: VGZ, TSX: VGZ) released a Mt Todd Gold Project development update on July 29, 2026, confirming that several key pre-construction milestones are advancing on schedule ahead of the company's participation at Australia's Diggers & Dealers Mining Forum in Kalgoorlie, Western Australia on August 3–5, 2026. Permit modification submissions for Mt Todd in the Northern Territory are progressing, with initial authorizations already granted and additional approvals expected in the second half of 2026 — final approvals are anticipated in 2027, setting the stage for detailed engineering and design to begin at that time, followed by an approximately 27-month construction and commissioning period. A dewatering program has been initiated at the Batman pit and tailings storage facility, a critical path item that reduces risk and demonstrates active site preparation ahead of the formal construction decision. Site layout design refinements are complete, and pre-design field investigations for the tailings storage facility are being prepared. Mt Todd is a very large gold project by any measure — more than 8 million ounces of measured and indicated resources in the Northern Territory — and has long been considered a potential acquisition target for a major gold producer seeking near-production scale assets in Australia. Vista Gold's decision to present at Diggers & Dealers, the premier Australian mining conference and deal forum, signals that the company is actively seeking to increase the project's profile with Australian institutional investors and potential strategic partners at a moment when gold is trading above $4,000/oz.

headline: EXPERTS: GOLD $3,900–$4,350 IN AUGUST — Fed Hawkish Hold Caps Rally; Payrolls August 7 Is The Break Catalyst
snippet: A CBS News August 1, 2026 expert panel consensus projects gold trading within a $3,900–$4,350 per ounce range for the month of August — a wide band reflecting genuine uncertainty about whether the Federal Reserve's hawkish hold will tip into an actual rate hike, or whether softening economic data will hand markets a dovish surprise. The floor of $3,900 corresponds to the level at which sovereign wealth funds and central bank gold demand has historically defended price on every dip in the past 18 months — a buyer of last resort dynamic that has truncated downside moves. The $4,350 ceiling aligns with the technical resistance from the January 2026 blow-off top and is where technical sellers have repeatedly capped rallies since February. The key variable separating these two outcomes is the August 7 non-farm payrolls print: a soft reading (sub-150,000 jobs, unemployment ticking up) would revive the rate-cut narrative, push the dollar lower, and likely launch gold quickly back toward $4,100–$4,200; a strong reading (200,000+, unemployment stable or declining) would validate the Fed's hawkish stance and potentially trigger a test of $4,000 psychological support. Expert commentary emphasizes that the bull case for gold remains structurally intact regardless of August's data outcome — central bank buying, geopolitical demand, and the long-term erosion of confidence in fiat currency policy are secular trends that short-term rate decisions cannot override. For retail investors in junior mining, the broader analyst takeaway is that producers trading at discounts to NAV based on $3,200 long-term gold assumptions are structurally mispriced in a $4,000+ gold environment — even if the stock market has been slow to rerate them.

headline: SILVER IN SIXTH DEFICIT YEAR HITS FED HEADWINDS — Three Inventories Falling Together; China Made It Strategic Jan 1
snippet: A July 29, 2026 FX Leaders technical and fundamental analysis flags that silver is navigating an unusual collision of long-term structural bullishness and near-term macro headwinds, with spot silver hovering near $57.40/oz as the Federal Reserve's hawkish July 29 hold strengthened the dollar and applied short-term pressure on the metal. The structural case is as strong as it has ever been: the Silver Institute projects 2026 will be the sixth consecutive year of supply-demand deficit, with the 2026 gap estimated at 46 million troy ounces — the result of sustained industrial demand growth from photovoltaics (China alone imported 790+ tonnes in early 2026, driven partly by solar panel manufacturing) and electronics, against mining supply constrained by declining grades and insufficient new project development. A critical detail that many retail investors have overlooked: China officially reclassified silver from an ordinary commodity to a strategic material on January 1, 2026 — a policy change that, combined with domestic hoarding incentives, has accelerated drawdowns of the three largest global silver inventories simultaneously: Shanghai Futures Exchange, COMEX, and LBMA stocks are all declining in concert, with nearly a billion ounces having vanished from visible stocks since 2021. The structural bull case for silver — and by extension for silver mining equities on the TSX-V and ASX — has never been better supported by fundamentals. What has suppressed prices is the strong dollar and Fed rate path uncertainty, both of which are data-dependent and could reverse quickly on a weak payrolls print.

headline: LUX COPPER BEGINS ALASKA EXPLORATION — 34% Cu Rock Chips, Ambler District; Maiden Drill Mid-August (ASX: LUX)
snippet: Lux Copper Corp. (ASX: LUX), a newly listed Australian junior, commenced field exploration operations in northwest Alaska's Ambler Mining District on July 31, 2026 — just two weeks after debuting on the ASX following an oversubscribed A$15 million IPO that closed in July. The company is advancing two highly prospective projects in the Ambler District: the Baird Project and the Ambler Project, both targeting district-scale copper-zinc systems in one of Alaska's most prospective but underexplored corridors. The Baird Project hosts surface rock chip samples returning up to 34.3% copper and 32.8% zinc — headline-grabbing grades that indicate near-surface massive sulphide mineralisation rather than typical low-grade disseminated copper. Historical drilling at the Baird Project returned 37.7 metres at 2.45% copper, including a 4.9-metre internal interval at 10.23% Cu — a grade and width profile consistent with a VMS (volcanic massive sulphide) system of economic interest. Aerial geophysics and LiDAR surveys are underway now, with maiden diamond drilling at the Baird Project targeted to commence in mid-August following the geophysics work. For investors tracking the Alaska mineral resource development cycle, the Ambler Mining District has attracted sustained interest from multiple majors and intermediates attracted by its documented copper, cobalt, and zinc endowment — but the region has historically been constrained by access infrastructure challenges that the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority is actively working to address. Lux Copper's freshly funded IPO cash provides a full funded pathway to maiden drilling, making the mid-August drill start a near-term catalyst investors can track in real time.
